nodes.name: crankmagic
nodes.description: A Commander deck workshop and a place to play: decks, library, explore and Play, all on Cloudflare at crankmagic.com, with invite-only accounts, live-first card data, and games run by CME, the CrankMagic Engine, in Durable Objects.

detail.what: The pages and modules that make CrankMagic, running on the reader's phone or computer. A deck, a library and Explore all work without an account.
A small script the browser keeps beside the app. It saves the app's files and the data sets so the app opens and works offline.
detail.today: Precaches the shell and the data files by their ?v= pins.
detail.final: Keeps the last good copy of each dated data set named by current.json, and a size-limited image cache.

detail.what: The browser's own database. It holds the library and, in the final state, the card records fetched from Scryfall with their lifetimes.
Cloudflare's sign-in gate in front of /api/*. It lets through only people on the Invited list and hands the Worker a signed token naming them.
detail.auth: Google sign-in; an emailed one-time code for library sync only
detail.owner: Rob manages the Invited list in the Zero Trust dashboard
detail.terms: The free plan caps Access at 50 people

detail.what: A second Access application, only for the AI routes. Google with passkey MFA where the plan offers it, and never the emailed code.
A small program at Cloudflare's edge. It answers /api/* for accounts, and in the final state also /data/* from R2, the table front door, imports and the AI door. Every other path is a plain file.
detail.protocol: HTTPS; bindings to D1, R2 and the game rooms
detail.auth: Checks the Access token again on every request: signature, audience, issuer, expiry and a named person
detail.plan: M2 adds /data/*, M3 rate limits and delete, M5 tables, M6 the AI door

detail.what: The released pages, scripts, styles and pictures, served straight from Cloudflare without running any code.
detail.policy: The security policy lets the page load scripts and fonts only from this site
detail.plan: Built from one commit of main by tools/release-pages.mjs

detail.what: Cloudflare's privacy-first page counts. Its beacon reports to this site's own address.
Cloudflare's SQL database. Production is `crankmagic`, staging is `crankmagic-staging`.
detail.protocol: A binding the Worker calls; nothing else reaches it
detail.plan: M5 adds tables and seats, M6 the AI allowlist and call log

detail.what: Cloudflare's file storage. It holds each good data run under a dated key, a small current.json naming the newest, the card definitions and the nightly database copy.
detail.plan: M2. Rob turns R2 on and makes its token
detail.terms: Free tier: 10 GB-month, 1 million writes and 10 million reads a month, free egress

detail.what: One Durable Object per match: a single place in the cloud that runs the engine, keeps the authoritative game and sends each seat only what that seat may see.
detail.plan: M5. Likely needs Workers Paid ($5 a month) once the engine's CPU per request passes 10 ms

detail.what: minorrob/mtg-deck-matrix, private. main holds everything; release/pages records each production build.
GitHub's runners. Today they run the test gate on every push. In the final state they also run the data refresh on a schedule and the weekly rules check.
detail.terms: A private repository gets 2,000 free minutes a month; CI plus the refresh is about 300 a month more

detail.what: Where Rob invites people, sets Email Routing and zone settings, and enters Worker secrets. These stay his, in a browser.
A Claude Code session in a cloud container. It builds, tests and deploys with an API credential the environment holds, so no step needs Rob's laptop.
detail.auth: An account-scoped Cloudflare API token, injected by the environment; never typed into chat

detail.what: The only public address. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards it to Rob; where it forwards is set in the dashboard and kept out of the repository.
Card records, prices, rulings and legality, one card at a time.
detail.live: Live: read when a card is opened or added
detail.terms: A descriptive User-Agent, about ten requests a second at most, and bulk files for bulk pulls

detail.what: cards.scryfall.io and svgs.scryfall.io: card pictures and mana symbols.
detail.live: Always live; never stored by us
detail.lifetime: The browser's HTTP cache, and the worker's image cache with a size limit

detail.what: Daily files of every card (oracle_cards, default_cards). The scheduled job reads them, never a reader's browser.
detail.terms: Scryfall asks that bulk pulls use these files

detail.what: Commander popularity, themes and which cards are played together.
detail.live: Stored: EDHREC has no public API and is not built for live traffic from an app
detail.refresh: Weekly, gently, by the scheduled job

detail.what: Precon decklists and set data, as bulk files.
A deck-building site. A deck link is read once and the result lands in the person's library.
detail.live: Live, through the Worker; never stored

detail.what: The Comprehensive Rules text, release notes and the Commander format page (banned list, Game Changers, brackets).
detail.live: Read at build time by the engine's tooling and when a case is adjudicated; never by a reader's browser
detail.terms: Wizards' texts are read and cited, not redistributed or committed

detail.what: Claude, for the Coach, LLM seats and card compilation. Reached only by the Worker's AI door and the compiler job.
detail.auth: A key held as a Worker secret; it never reaches a browser

detail.what: The identity provider behind Cloudflare Access. CrankMagic never sees a password.
After Access signs a person in, sends them back to the app. Only a fragment of this app may be the destination.
Who is signed in, and the library version their devices converge on.
The head: the newest version of this person's library.
Saves a version. The head moves only from where this device left it; otherwise the answer is 409 and the person chooses.
Files this device's version without moving the head: the side a person did not keep, held 30 days.
The versions held, newest first, without their bodies.
One version with its body, only ever the asking person's own.
Deletes the person's snapshots, head and user row after a type-to-confirm dialog. Removing them from Access is Rob's runbook step.
Stores account-level switches, such as 'Tell me when Play is ready'.
Serves current.json (short cache) and the dated data files (long cache) from R2.
Fetches a deck from an Archidekt link, with a size limit, and stores nothing.
Creates a table and its game room; returns the invite link and QR.
Joins or leaves a seat, handing it to the signed-in person. Identity stays out of the engine.
Upgrades to a WebSocket and hands it to the table's game room; a reconnect gets a fresh permitted view.
The AI door: checks the allowlist and the spend cap, calls the model, and logs the call.
A small file naming the newest good data run: each file's dated key, checksum and date. The app reads it in place of ?v= pins.
Each good run's files under data/<date>/. The last seven runs are kept, so a bad day rolls back by rewriting current.json.
detail.lifetime: Long cache; a dated file never changes

detail.what: The engine's card definitions, versioned, loaded by a game room for the version the game pinned.
A nightly export of the D1 database, beside D1's own Time Travel.
detail.plan: M3, once M2 turns R2 on

detail.what: The class each match runs in. It holds the authoritative state, applies each action through CME, writes the journal and checkpoints through the storage adapter, and sends each seat its own view.
detail.plan: M4 builds the storage adapter; M5 builds the room

detail.what: One row per person who has signed in.
detail.source: Cloudflare Access names the person; the Worker writes the row

nodes.name: email
nodes.meaning: Who they are, lower-cased, from the Access token.

nodes.name: seen_at
nodes.meaning: When they were last seen, moved at most hourly to save writes.

nodes.name: notify_play
nodes.meaning: The 'Tell me when Play is ready' switch.

detail.what: Saved versions of a person's library. Each is the app's own checksummed backup, gzipped by the browser. The Worker never opens one.
detail.lifetime: The newest 20 everyday versions; a displaced or kept version for 30 days

nodes.name: id
nodes.meaning: The version's id, minted by the Worker.

nodes.name: parent_id
nodes.meaning: The version the device started from; empty for a first save.

nodes.name: kind
nodes.meaning: sync, displaced (replaced by a choice) or kept (the side not chosen).

nodes.name: revision
nodes.meaning: The device's own revision number when it saved.

nodes.name: checksum
nodes.meaning: The backup's SHA-256; the browser verifies it on the way back.

nodes.name: size
nodes.meaning: Length of the body in characters.

nodes.name: body
nodes.meaning: The whole library, gzipped and base64-encoded.

detail.what: For each person, the version every device should converge on. It moves only from where a device left it.

nodes.name: id
nodes.meaning: The table's id, in its invite link.

nodes.name: room_id
nodes.meaning: The Durable Object running the match.

nodes.name: rules
nodes.meaning: The table's rules: bracket, timers, who may join.

detail.what: Who sits where: a person, the house pilot, or an LLM seat. Invitations are seats with no person yet.

nodes.name: user_id
nodes.meaning: The person in it; empty for an AI seat or an open invitation.

nodes.name: invite_token
nodes.meaning: The link or QR code's token for an open human seat.

detail.what: The people Rob allows to use AI features. Separate from the invite list.

nodes.name: note
nodes.meaning: Why they are on the list.

detail.what: A log of every AI call: who, what for, tokens and cost.

nodes.name: prompt_digest
nodes.meaning: A hash of what was sent, not the text.

detail.what: The library as one record: every collection below, a schema version and a revision. A change is saved with its receipt and an undo point in one transaction.

nodes.name: revision
nodes.meaning: Goes up by one with every saved change.

detail.what: The cards this library knows, as references: the facts live on the Card record, read from the catalog.

nodes.name: shipped
nodes.meaning: True when the shipped record set carries the card, so only its identity is kept.

detail.what: Physical copies, in groups: owned, ordered, watching or to buy, where they sit, and which deck slot they fill.

nodes.name: allocation.deckId
nodes.meaning: The deck these copies are reserved for.

detail.what: Decks: a commander, a list of slots, a definition (bracket, budget, style) and a status from draft to final.

nodes.name: version
nodes.meaning: Goes up when the list is finalized.

nodes.name: groupId
nodes.meaning: The collection group the deck belongs to.

detail.what: A deck's hundred: one row per card it calls for. Held inside its deck.

nodes.name: deck
nodes.meaning: The deck it belongs to (it is stored inside the deck).

nodes.name: committed
nodes.meaning: True once the deck is finalized and the slot counts toward To Buy.

detail.what: Collection groups: Main Deck, Bench, To Trade, To Buy, and the person's own.
Measure reports filed under a deck.
Games played with a deck. In the final state a cloud game files its own record here, with the data version it pinned.

nodes.name: dataVersion
nodes.meaning: The card data and definitions the game pinned.

detail.what: The person's settings that travel with the library.

nodes.name: starterGroups
nodes.meaning: Whether the starter groups were offered.

nodes.name: budgetCap
nodes.meaning: The budget a new deck starts with.

detail.what: Each card record fetched from Scryfall, kept in the browser with its fetch time.
detail.live: Live first; this is the second choice
detail.lifetime: 7 days for a record, 24 hours for its price, and at once when a set releases
detail.terms: Scryfall's content, cached for the reader only

nodes.name: record
nodes.meaning: The card as Scryfall returned it.

nodes.name: etag
nodes.meaning: Lets the browser ask 'has it changed?' instead of downloading again.

detail.what: The service worker's copies of the app and the data sets, so the app opens offline.
detail.final: Keyed by the dated files current.json names; the last good copy stays

nodes.name: version
nodes.meaning: Which build or data run it belongs to.

detail.what: The index of the newest good data run. The app, the Settings page and a game room all read it.
detail.refresh: Rewritten last by each good run

nodes.name: date
nodes.meaning: The run's date; a game pins it.

nodes.name: files[].madeAt
nodes.meaning: When that set was last refreshed; Settings › About shows it.

detail.what: One dated snapshot of the card records the app carries, with prices, for bulk arithmetic: a deck's cost to finish, the buy list's total, the cap checks.
detail.today: data/cards.json, a pinned static file refreshed by hand
detail.terms: Scryfall's data; bulk file, descriptive User-Agent

detail.what: Every Commander-legal card's name and identity, so search and pickers work without 31,830 requests.
The rules text of all 31,830 cards the engine knows, as of a stated date, so a game is deterministic and replays identically.
The engine's definition of each card, hand-authored for the seven decks and compiled for the rest, each checked against its oracle text.

nodes.name: version
nodes.meaning: The definition's version; a game pins it.

nodes.name: script
nodes.meaning: The card's behavior in the engine's vocabulary.

nodes.name: status
nodes.meaning: supported, or refused with what it lacks.

detail.what: For every card in the pool, whether the engine can play it yet and, if not, the construct it lacks.
detail.today: data/engine/support.json; every row unsupported until definitions land

nodes.name: tier
nodes.meaning: How much new engine work the card needs.

detail.what: Our own derived data: how every card relates to every other, behind Explore. Computed across every card, so it must be stored.
detail.today: data/graph.json (16 MB) and data/graph-played.json (21 MB), near Cloudflare's 25 MiB file cap
detail.plan: M2 splits graph-played before it reaches the cap

nodes.name: facets
nodes.meaning: Its roles, such as ramp or removal.

nodes.name: played
nodes.meaning: Cards played with it, from EDHREC co-play.

detail.what: A nightly export of D1, beside Time Travel.

nodes.name: tables
nodes.meaning: users, snapshots, heads and the rest.

detail.what: The authoritative game: the seed, the turn, every zone and a hash of it all. Only the room holds it.

nodes.name: room_id
nodes.meaning: The room this game lives in.

nodes.name: seed

nodes.name: zones

nodes.name: dataVersion
nodes.meaning: The oracle snapshot and definitions pinned at start.

nodes.name: action
nodes.meaning: What they did, with its targets.

detail.what: A saved copy of the state every so often, so a room resumes identically after a restart, written through the storage adapter.

nodes.name: state
nodes.meaning: The whole state at that point.

detail.what: Each seat's connection and the view it may see. A seat's view never includes another seat's hand.

nodes.name: connected

nodes.name: Arrives at crankmagic.com and sees the landing page.
Starts a deck by pasting a list or naming a commander.
Browses Library and Explore; pictures load from Scryfall.
Everything is kept in this browser. Signing in is optional.
Signs in with Google through Access.
Edits a deck on the laptop; the library saves itself to the cloud.
Opens the phone; the same library is there.
Both changed offline: asked which to keep, and the other is held 30 days.
Checks Settings › About for how old each data set is.
Opens a card on the phone and sees today's price and its age.
Signal drops; the library and cached cards still work.
Adds it to To Buy; the deck's cost to finish updates from the price snapshot.
A host and an invited guest
The host creates a table and picks a mat.
Invites a guest by e-mail, link or QR.
The guest signs in and takes the seat.
Every human seat ready: a ten-second countdown, then the game starts.
They play over the table's WebSocket; a dropped phone reconnects to a fresh view.
The result files itself under each player's deck.
A player with an AI seat
Fills a seat with the house pilot, which costs nothing and sees only its seat.
Or, if allowlisted, an LLM seat through the AI door.
A spend meter shows what the game has cost.
Asks the Coach what to do next.
Invites a person by adding their e-mail to the Access Invited list.
Enters secrets himself: the data job's token in GitHub, the AI key as a Worker secret.
Approves a plan; a cloud session builds, walks and deploys it to staging.
Gets an alert on errors or sync conflicts.

edges.action: A change is made: a card bought, a deck finalized.
Saved in IndexedDB with its receipt and an undo point, before it shows.
Signed in, the request carries the Access token.
The library, gzipped and checksummed, is sent with the version it started from.
Stored as a new version.
The head moves only if no other device saved in between; otherwise the person chooses.
Another device reads the head and restores it, checking the checksum.
A card is opened or added.
If a fresh copy is in the reader's cache, it is used and checked in the background.
Otherwise Scryfall is asked, one card, within its rate.
The record and its price arrive.
A card is drawn on screen.
Its picture is loaded from cards.scryfall.io.
Kept in the browser's caches, with a size limit.
On schedule, tools/refresh.mjs runs.
Reads every card and its prices.
Weekly: ranks and co-play, gently.
Weekly: precon decklists.
Uploads the files under today's date.
Then rewrites current.json to name them. The last seven runs are kept.
The Worker serves them, current.json on a short cache.
The service worker keeps the last good copy for offline use.
The oracle text of every Commander-legal card.
A dated snapshot of 31,830 cards.
The ledger says which cards the engine can play.
Definitions: the seven decks by hand (M4), then every card compiled and checked (M7).
Published, versioned.
A room loads the version its game pinned.
A player acts: casts a spell, chooses a target.
Over the table's WebSocket.
The room applies it through CME; every choice is offered to its owner.
Written to the journal with a hash.
Checkpointed through the storage adapter.
Each seat gets its own view; no seat sees another's hand.
At the end, the game's record is filed under the deck and syncs.
The Coach is asked, or an LLM seat takes its turn.
The AI door's own sign-in: Google with MFA.
The Worker receives the call.
Checks the person is allowed and under their cap.
Uses the key held as a Worker secret.
Calls the model.
Logs who, what for, tokens and cost.
The Comprehensive Rules, then the card's rulings, then the release notes, then the Commander page.
Rules are cited by number against a stated date.
A scheduled check lists the rules that moved.
A dated banned list checks decks at prepare.
A deck link is pasted.
The Worker fetches it with a size limit.
Archidekt returns the list.
It becomes a deck in the library.
The database.
Exported each night.
Kept as a dated copy.
A commit of main.
The gate runs.
tools/release-pages.mjs builds it and the acceptance walk passes on it.
wrangler deploys with the deploy credential.
Staging first, then production on Rob's go.
